# External trace proof: TodoMVC

The target is the public React [TodoMVC demo](https://demo.playwright.dev/todomvc/), hosted by Playwright. It is independent of this repository's detective-agency app. The tests import only `@playwright/test`; they do not use the crime scene, fault-injection fixture, forensics attachments, injected labels or trained classifier.

On 2026-11-10, Chromium ran [todomvc.spec.ts](todomvc.spec.ts) against that live application with Playwright 1.64.1. Both tests intentionally fail after successfully adding one task:

| Capture | Intended test mistake | Observed diagnosis | Reports |
|---|---|---|---|
| [count.zip](../../agent/test/fixtures/external/count.zip) | Expect two tasks after adding one | `assertion_mismatch`, including expected/received values | [JSON](reports/count.json), [Markdown](reports/count.md), [SARIF](reports/count.sarif) |
| [locator.zip](../../agent/test/fixtures/external/locator.zip) | Click a nonexistent `Archive tasks` button | `locator_not_found`, including the timed-out locator | [JSON](reports/locator.json), [Markdown](reports/locator.md), [SARIF](reports/locator.sarif) |

The original trace ZIP bytes are retained as captured; report fingerprints refer to these files. Their metadata includes capture-machine source paths. Each trace records a single attempt, so it contains no evidence of retry behavior. Screenshots and source embedding were disabled; DOM snapshots, network activity and runner errors remain in the ZIP. The analyzer uses trace metadata and does not depend on supplemental files generated by Playwright.

To inspect a capture manually:

```sh
npx playwright show-trace agent/test/fixtures/external/count.zip
npm run analyze-trace -- agent/test/fixtures/external/count.zip --format markdown
```

To repeat the live experiment:

```sh
npx playwright install chromium
npm run proof:external
```

The proof command runs the tests, verifies that setup succeeded and both intended failures occurred, analyzes each ZIP, asserts the diagnoses, and writes JSON, Markdown and SARIF to `.scratch/external-proof/reports/`. Playwright displays two expected failures; the wrapper returns success only after checking the diagnoses. A changed or unavailable demo makes the proof fail instead of accepting a different failure. It does not overwrite the committed captures or example reports.

Normal `npm test` uses only the committed captures, including end-to-end CLI checks for all three formats. No browser or network connection is needed for those checks.

These two known test mistakes prove ingestion and symptom diagnosis on another application. They do not establish accuracy for real application defects or production outages. The analyzer reports the mismatch or missing locator and requests review; it cannot infer from the trace alone that these mistakes were intentional, and never edits assertions or substitutes controls automatically.
